title: DOM XSS via jQuery .html() on location.hash
learning_objectives: Identify a DOM-based XSS where a client-side router writes location.hash into the page with jQuery .html() (innerHTML)
Understand why innerHTML will not run a bare <script> but WILL run event-handler attributes on freshly parsed elements
Use as the reliable innerHTML execution primitive
Read document.cookie from the victim's browser and exfiltrate the non-HttpOnly session to an OOB collector
See that the fix is .text() (or a sanitiser), never .html() on untrusted routing input
flag_hint: Submit /# (URL-encoded) to POST /report; the admin bot's jQuery .html() runs it, exfiltrating its session cookie. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The jQuery .html() DOM-XSS pattern, abstracted for local Docker. Uses current jQuery 3.7.1 rather than the catalog's 3.4.1 — the taught flaw is the app's own .html(untrusted) misuse (identical across versions), and a non-CVE'd jQuery keeps the Trivy gate honest and avoids an unintended solve path.
